evidence: Across all three fixed N=5000 graphs, interior mean IPR is smallest near a/s_ref=0.25-0.5 and rises strongly between a/s_ref=1 and 8.
At large a, upper-edge centers preferentially have positive xi and lower-edge centers negative xi, while their degrees remain above average.
The completed pilot has two potentials but only one graph per model, so graph-level and finite-size uncertainty are missing.
Radius-two local reference states usually fail the residual criterion; follow-up tunneling work must change or enrich the approximate-state basis before interpreting coupling ratios.

operator.xi: iid NumPy Generator.uniform(-1,1), paired across a within a sweep

priority_graph_replication.purpose: add graph-level uncertainty at the pilot size before any transition claim
priority_graph_replication.execution: bounded job arrays with per-amplitude checkpoint/resume; retain the completed cached graph as the first graph-level observation

gated_finite_size_followup.gate: run if the graph-replicated summaries retain a rise in interior IPR between a/s_ref=1 and 8
gated_finite_size_followup.reason: it has the lowest baseline interior IPR and the cleanest large-a potential-sign selection in the pilot
analysis_rules: form spacings within each graph and potential realization only
keep rank windows separate from fixed-energy or quantile windows
report graph-level and potential-level uncertainty separately
do not label a critical disorder or mobility edge unless the trend is stable across sizes and graphs
full-spectrum claims require full spectral coverage; partial window runs must be labeled partial

required_changes: increase or adapt local neighborhoods until residual convergence is demonstrated
include additional resonant centers when the two-state Gram or residual checks fail
compare radius and eta sensitivity before interpreting Schur-mediated coupling
retain failed residual cases as inconclusive rather than as measured tunneling evidence

small_world.reason: No explicit distinct SW generator exists in the audited repository; do not introduce Watts-Strogatz without a supplied definition.
